prompt:
Create exactly ONE finished, flat, opaque landscape 16:9 community cultural-event poster for adult residents, used on community digital screens. Use case: ads-marketing. A friendly invitation to a single connected architecture photography exhibition and guided space talk, welcoming people without architectural knowledge. This is a clean raster poster artwork, with no surrounding room, frame, mockup, contact sheet, inset alternative poster or comparison panel.
요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Whole visual design: bold flat optical architectural graphics. The upper approximately 61% is a generous warm ivory information field, with two clear side-by-side information groups. The lower approximately 39% is a continuous full-width architectural light study. Use deep blue-black for all type and structural shadow, warm ivory for walls and the background, vivid yellow-green for planes of sunlight. Limit the colors, keep strong neutral text contrast. Smooth flat color fills, precise edges; no texture, grain, ink bleed, gradients, folded paper, duct tape, shiny 3D letters or fabricated craft finish.

Lower image: a fictional ordinary interior seen as a long horizontal wall-and-floor band. Thick walls, deep rectangular window reveals, visible jambs and sills. Openings repeat across the width, cropped at the far left and right so the architecture continues beyond the frame. Their yellow-green light planes pass coherently through the openings and stretch diagonally onto the floor, making long blue-black shadows and a lively rhythm of light boundaries. Maintain clearly corresponding opening directions, wall thickness, and floor-light edges. Draw actual architectural forms and spatial depth using flat polygons, not letters, glyphs, tiny symbols, arbitrary abstract bars or an icon. The whole bottom band must carry the pleasure of observing architectural form and light; no identifiable real building or institution. No people needed.

Typography: crisp, straight, contemporary Korean gothic sans serif, flat and highly legible. Preserve Korean character proportions, counters, consonant/vowel distinctions, natural word spaces, digits and punctuation. All eleven supplied copy entries must appear once each, readable when the entire poster is viewed at 720 pixels wide. Keep each entry on one line, with useful line spacing, and generous distance from the picture boundary. No extra text or diagram labels, no logos, pseudo-print, watermark, QR, URL or invented application details.

Layout in proportional 720×405 viewing coordinates, serving the clear relationships rather than a rigid diagram: left group starts near x24, right schedule group near x444, margins about 24. Korean title at upper left near y24, visually about 36px at this viewing size and bold; English name beneath it near y79 at about 19px, event description beneath near y107 at 19px. The English name must not become the only huge anchor. Upper-right date and time near y24 and y61, about 27px bold, with venue and entry time beneath near y126 and y154, about 20px. Free admission/guidance and reservation/capacity in the left group near y157 and y184, about 20px. The two visiting/welcome sentences occupy a broad right-side area starting around x355 near y194 and y218, about 18px, so these Korean lines are not squeezed into narrow columns. All practical copy finishes above the architectural band beginning about y248. Left title and right schedule share the top edge; title → event identity → date/time → venue/entry → free/guidance/reservation → visiting/welcome forms an easy reading route, followed by the window-and-shadow rhythm below.
